newsitem.title: SWEDEN: No confidence vote knocks Swedish ruling party-poll.
newsitem.headline: No confidence vote knocks Swedish ruling party-poll.

text.p: Sweden's ruling Social Democrats fell in popularity according to the first public poll conducted since opposition parties mounted an unsuccessful vote of no confidence against Prime Minister Goran Persson.

The survey by the Swedish Institute of Public Research and Opinion (SIFO), published on Sunday, showed that support for the Social Democrats had slipped by 1.2 percent to 32.7 percent in November compared to a month ago.

But the opposition parties that organised the no confidence vote against Persson on November 22 for seemingly complimentary comments he made about China's political stability during a Beijing visit, did not benefit from the move either.
The Liberals, who spearheaded the vote, saw their share of the vote dip by 0.2 percentage points to 6.1 percent.
Support for the Moderates in the poll of 4,698 people slipped 0.9 percentage points to 26.4 percent while the Christian Democrats remained unchanged at 4.7 percent.
The parties to win most popularity in the poll were the Left Party, whose support rose 1.8 percentage points to 13.4 percent and the Greens, who gained 0.5 and rose to 8.1 percent.

These parties had managed to keep some distance from the vote against Persson, who came to power in Sweden as leader of the Social Democrats in March after former prime minister Ingvar Carlsson retired from politics.
